SMTO-CFG-0085 — SMTO tried to add a built-in helper Skill on its own

GUID: ab9c0548-7bcd-591f-9cf3-2d343787c387
Slug: capability-activation-dependency-only-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • Some Skills are built-in helpers that SMTO adds automatically with the Skills that need them. The Agent tried to turn one on by itself, which isn't allowed. Nothing changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Watch the Task. If it keeps working after a Capability request blocked note, you don't need to do anything. SMTO tells the Agent to use the main Skill instead, and the helper comes with it.
  2. If the Task stops, open Capabilities by the message box and set the main Skill the work needs to Always. Turning on the main Skill brings in the helper Skills it depends on.
  3. Check which steps the stopped Task already finished, then send a new request for the rest. Capability changes apply to the next request, and checking first avoids repeating finished work.

What success looks like

  • The Task keeps working with the main Skill, without another Capability request blocked note.

If it still fails

  • Send Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO. Helpers such as Task Context are built in and marked Always enabled, so don't look for a setting to switch them on separately.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Activation classification rejected the requested Skill because its selection mode is dependency_only; it is available only through a parent Skill's declared tool dependencies (capability_activation.dependency_only_invalid).

What this means

  • The requested Skill is marked dependency_only in its registry selection metadata. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • The requested Skill is marked dependency_only in its registry selection metadata.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the parent Skill's declared tool dependencies and accepted authority.

How to fix it

  • Request the parent Skill whose uses_tools includes this dependency instead of the internal Skill (classify in src/agent_runtime/native/capability_activation.py; ROUTING in src/agent_runtime/skills/selection.py), and confirm that parent is inside the run's accepted ceiling.
  • This internal Skill is available only through its parent capability dependencies.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • The internal dependency is included only through a permitted supported parent capability.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
